verdict.rationale: Simular says Sai can rerun a taught task on a schedule, and its REST API, Python SDK and MCP server let external code send tasks to Sai for non-interactive runs. However, scheduling appears only as a single marketing line with no configuration docs. The API trigger is documented for cloud Windows computers, not explicitly for the user's own devices. Missing for 10: documented schedule configuration (cadence, cron, management), native event triggers or inbound webhooks, confirmation that API or scheduled runs target BYOD devices, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, I can schedule a device task or trigger it from an external event, not only run it interactively

citations.quote: Teach it once, and Sai reruns on a schedule, getting more reliable and cost-efficient each time.
Developers can drive Sai from their own code or coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) with the Sai API: send a task in plain language, and Sai completes it on a cloud Windows computer.
gives developers, their code and their coding agents the same autonomous computer through a REST API, a Python SDK and an MCP server.
